$comment: Conversation scenarios for the demo, scheduling constraints, and age rules. The runner checks each structured response and validates every candidate with the deterministic engine.

scenarios.why: The exact hero demo: rainy Tokyo afternoon, infant along, fixed 18:00 dinner. If this regresses, the pitch dies.

turns.say: We have about four hours before dinner. It's raining and our eight-month-old is with us. We'd like something genuinely local and cultural, around ¥15,000. Nothing too crowded.
Actually, the baby just fell asleep. Quiet matters more than the budget now.

scenarios.why: The guest asks for something deterministically impossible (outdoor cycling, pouring rain, infant). The engine would catch it — the model must not propose it, and must say why honestly.

turns.say: It's pouring but we really want to be outdoors on bikes this afternoon with the baby. Around ¥20,000. Can you make it work?

scenarios.why: Age rules are deterministic. A sake tasting with a child in tow must never appear as a candidate.

turns.say: I'd love to do a sake tasting around three o'clock — our six-year-old nephew is with us today as well as the baby.

scenarios.why: The torture conversation: outing changes must supersede old constraints — no stale quiet=5 haunting a celebration, no party-size contamination.

turns.say: Three adults — me and two friends — with about four hours before dinner. We'd love something fun.
Actually, I'm feeling a little sad today. I think I'd rather do something calming, just by myself.
So my sister's going to visit and I kind of want to take her somewhere fun on Saturday. It'll be just the two of us, no baby along.
Oh and I just got promoted, so somewhere really nice to celebrate would be great.
